site.title: Free PDF & Print Tools Directory
site.description: No-account, free tools for merge, split, compress, sign, fill forms, large print, and ebook conversion. No affiliate links.

tools.name: PDF24 Tools — Merge PDF
tools.cost: Free — no account required
tools.platform: Web (any browser); optional Windows desktop tool
steps: Open the PDF24 Merge PDF tool.
Drag your PDFs into the drop zone, or click to choose files.
Drag files to reorder them, then click Merge PDF.
Download the merged PDF.
tools.about: Browser-based merger. Uploaded files are deleted from PDF24's servers after a short time.

tools.name: iLovePDF — Merge PDF
tools.cost: Free tier — no account required for basic use
steps: Open iLovePDF Merge PDF.
Select your PDFs or drag them into the drop zone.
Click Merge PDF.
Download the merged PDF.
tools.about: Free tier merges files without an account; daily usage limits apply.

tools.name: qpdf — Merge (command line)
tools.cost: Free and open source — no account required
steps: Install qpdf (brew install qpdf, apt install qpdf, or the Windows installer).
Run: qpdf --empty --pages file1.pdf file2.pdf -- merged.pdf
Find merged.pdf in the same folder.
tools.about: Lightweight CLI for structural PDF changes. Great for scripting and batch work.

tools.name: pdftk / pdftk-java — Merge (command line)
tools.cost: Free — no account required
steps: Install pdftk-java (the maintained rebuild of pdftk).
Run: pdftk file1.pdf file2.pdf cat output merged.pdf
Find merged.pdf in the same folder.
tools.about: Classic PDF toolkit. pdftk-java keeps the original pdftk command working on modern systems.

tools.name: PDF Arranger — Merge & Rearrange Pages
tools.cost: Free and open source — no account required
steps: Install PDF Arranger from Flathub or your package manager.
Drag PDFs into the left sidebar.
Drag pages between files to reorder them.
Save the result as a new PDF.
tools.about: Graphical tool for merging, splitting, rotating, and cropping PDF pages.

tools.name: PDF24 Tools — Split PDF
tools.cost: Free — no account required
steps: Open the PDF24 Split PDF tool.
Upload your PDF.
Choose extract page ranges or split into single pages, then click Split.
Download the split files (or the ZIP).
tools.about: Browser-based splitter. Uploaded files are deleted from PDF24's servers after a short time.

tools.name: iLovePDF — Split PDF
tools.cost: Free tier — no account required for basic use
steps: Open iLovePDF Split PDF.
Upload your PDF and choose how to split it.
Click Split PDF.
Download the results.
tools.about: Free tier splits files without an account; daily usage limits apply.

tools.name: qpdf — Split (command line)
tools.cost: Free and open source — no account required
steps: Install qpdf.
Run: qpdf --pages input.pdf 1-5,6-10 -- part.pdf
Or run: qpdf --split-pages input.pdf page to split every page into its own file.
tools.about: Fast CLI splitting by page range.

tools.name: pdftk / pdftk-java — Burst / Split (command line)
tools.cost: Free — no account required
steps: Install pdftk-java.
Run: pdftk input.pdf burst
Pages are saved as pg_0001.pdf, pg_0002.pdf, etc.
To grab a range: pdftk input.pdf cat 1-5 output part.pdf
tools.about: burst splits a PDF into one file per page; cat selects page ranges.

tools.name: PDF Arranger — Delete / Extract Pages
tools.cost: Free and open source — no account required
steps: Install PDF Arranger from Flathub or your package manager.
Open your PDF.
Select pages to delete or drag them out into a new file.
Save the result.
tools.about: Visual page manager for splitting PDFs by hand.

tools.name: PDF24 Tools — Compress PDF
tools.cost: Free — no account required
steps: Open the PDF24 Compress PDF tool.
Upload your PDF and pick a compression strength.
Click Compress PDF.
Download the smaller PDF.
tools.about: Browser-based compressor. Uploaded files are deleted from PDF24's servers after a short time.

tools.name: iLovePDF — Compress PDF
tools.cost: Free tier — no account required for basic use
steps: Open iLovePDF Compress PDF.
Upload your PDF and choose a compression level.
Click Compress PDF.
Download the compressed file.
tools.about: Free tier compresses files without an account; daily usage limits apply.

tools.name: Ghostscript — Compress (command line)
tools.cost: Free and open source — no account required
steps: Install Ghostscript (gs).
Run: gs -sDEVICE=pdfwrite -dCompatibilityLevel=1.4 -dPDFSETTINGS=/ebook -dNOPAUSE -dQUIET -dBATCH -sOutputFile=compressed.pdf input.pdf
Use /screen for smallest files, /ebook for balanced, /prepress for highest quality.
tools.about: Industry-standard CLI for PDF compression and conversion.

tools.name: Sejda — Compress PDF
tools.cost: Free tier (3 tasks per hour, up to 200 pages) — no account required
steps: Open Sejda Compress PDF.
Upload your PDF and choose a compression level.
Click Compress PDF.
Download the compressed file.
tools.about: Free daily limits apply; no account needed for basic use.

tools.name: PDF24 Tools — Sign PDF
tools.cost: Free — no account required
steps: Open the PDF24 Sign PDF tool.
Upload your PDF and add your signature (draw, type, or upload an image).
Place the signature on the page, then click Sign.
Download the signed PDF.
tools.about: Adds a visual signature to pages. Uploaded files are deleted from PDF24's servers after a short time.

tools.name: LibreOffice Draw — Sign & Fill
tools.cost: Free and open source — no account required
steps: Open the PDF in LibreOffice Draw.
Insert > Image to place a scanned signature, or draw with the toolbar tools.
File > Export as PDF to save the signed file.
Close and keep the exported PDF.
tools.about: Desktop office suite that can open, annotate, sign, and re-export PDFs.

tools.name: Master PDF Editor (free version) — Sign
tools.cost: Free for non-commercial use — no account required
steps: Download and install the free version of Master PDF Editor.
Open your PDF and place a signature with the annotation tools.
Save the signed PDF.
tools.about: The free version is for non-commercial use and includes viewing, filling, and signing.

tools.name: Xodo — Fill & Sign Online
tools.cost: Free — no account required for basic use
steps: Open Xodo's online PDF tools.
Upload your PDF and add a signature or initials.
Place them on the page, then download the signed file.
tools.about: Free online viewer with fill-and-sign features; account optional.

tools.name: Firefox / Chrome / Edge — Fill PDF Forms (built in)
tools.cost: Free — no account required
steps: Open the PDF in Firefox, Chrome, or Edge.
Click each form field and type your answers.
Print or choose Save as PDF to keep your filled copy.
Note: this works on fillable forms; flat PDFs need LibreOffice Draw or PDF24.
tools.about: Every modern browser can fill fillable PDF forms and save or print the result.

tools.name: LibreOffice Draw — Fill PDF Forms
tools.cost: Free and open source — no account required
steps: Open the PDF in LibreOffice Draw.
Click form fields to type, or insert text boxes on flat PDFs.
File > Export as PDF to save the filled file.
tools.about: Good for forms that browsers can't handle, plus adding text to any page.

tools.name: pdftk / pdftk-java — Fill Forms (command line)
tools.cost: Free — no account required
steps: Export an FDF data file from the form, or write one by hand.
Run: pdftk form.pdf fill_form data.fdf output filled.pdf
Check filled.pdf for your entered values.
tools.about: Batch-fills form fields from an FDF data file without opening a GUI.

tools.name: Sejda — Fill & Sign PDF Forms
tools.cost: Free tier — no account required for basic use
steps: Open Sejda's Fill and Sign PDF tool.
Upload your PDF, type into fields, and add a signature if needed.
Click Apply, then download the filled PDF.
tools.about: Online form filling with free daily limits; no account needed for basic use.

tools.name: Browser Print — Large Print via Scale
tools.cost: Free — no account required
steps: Open the PDF in Firefox, Chrome, or Edge.
Press Ctrl+P (or Cmd+P on Mac) to open Print.
Set Scale / Custom to 150% or 200%, and pick your paper size.
Print, or choose Save as PDF to create a large-print copy.
tools.about: The fastest no-install way to make a large-print copy of any PDF.

tools.name: PDF24 Tools — Scale / Resize Pages
tools.cost: Free — no account required
steps: Open the PDF24 Scale PDF tool.
Upload your PDF and enter a scale percentage (for example 140% for large print).
Click Scale, then download the enlarged pages.
tools.about: Permanently scales pages up so every printout is large print.

tools.name: Ghostscript — Large Print Rescale (command line)
tools.cost: Free and open source — no account required
steps: Install Ghostscript (gs).
Run: gs -sDEVICE=pdfwrite -dDEVICEWIDTHPOINTS=1224 -dDEVICEHEIGHTPOINTS=1584 -dPDFFitPage -dNOPAUSE -dQUIET -dBATCH -sOutputFile=largeprint.pdf input.pdf
That scales US Letter up to about 150% (1224 x 1584 points). Adjust dimensions for other sizes.
tools.about: CLI approach for batch large-print rescaling of many PDFs.

tools.name: Calibre — Convert PDF to EPUB / MOBI / AZW3
tools.cost: Free and open source — no account required
steps: Install Calibre.
Add your PDF to the Calibre library.
Select the book, click Convert books, and choose EPUB, MOBI, or AZW3 as the output format.
Save to disk or send to your ereader.
tools.about: The most popular free ebook manager; handles PDF-to-ebook conversion with metadata and cover support.

tools.name: LibreOffice Writer — Open PDF, Export EPUB
tools.cost: Free and open source — no account required
steps: Open the PDF in LibreOffice Writer.
Fix text and layout as needed.
File > Export As > Export as EPUB.
Save the EPUB file.
tools.about: Simple route from PDF to EPUB for text-heavy documents.

tools.name: Sigil — EPUB Editor (clean up converted ebooks)
tools.cost: Free and open source — no account required
steps: Open your converted EPUB in Sigil.
Fix formatting, add a cover image, and edit book metadata.
Save the EPUB and check it in an ereader app.
tools.about: WYSIWYG EPUB editor for polishing ebooks after conversion.
